title: Fat Bear Week: Vote for the Chubbiest Champ!
summary:
Imagine a bear so round it looks like a fuzzy brown beach ball. That's the goal of Fat Bear Week! From September 22 to 29, 2026, fans everywhere vote for the chubbiest brown bear in Alaska's Katmai National Park.

Katmai is huge — 4.1 million acres of volcanoes, rivers, and forests. About 2,200 brown bears live there, gobbling salmon from the rivers. Bears need lots of fat to survive the long, cold winter.

The contest started in 2014. Park Ranger Mike Fitz saw two photos of the same bear — one from June, one from September. The bear looked completely different! He turned the idea into a one-day Facebook event called "Fat Bear Tuesday." The next year, it became a whole week. In 2025, more than 1.7 million votes came in from over 100 countries!

How does it work? Each day, fans vote in a head-to-head matchup. The bear with more votes moves on. The last bear standing wins.

This year, 16 bears are in the running. Bear 32, called Chunk, is back to defend his title after recovering from a broken jaw. Bear 164, or Bucky, can snatch leaping salmon right out of the air. And Bear 132 is competing while raising three cubs!

Who will win? The final round is September 29. Cast your vote!
why_it_matters: Learning why bears must get fat reminds kids how animals get ready for hard seasons — just like people prepare for things they know are coming.

background_read: Katmai National Park (a big wild park in Alaska, in the far northwest of the United States) is home to about 2,200 brown bears.
Every summer, salmon (a kind of fish that swims up rivers) fill the park's rivers, and the bears eat and eat to build up body fat.
When winter comes and food is hard to find, bears go into hibernation — a deep sleep that lasts for months — living off the fat they stored.
Article_Structure: WHO: Fans around the world vote for the chubbiest brown bear in Katmai National Park, Alaska.
WHAT: A yearly online contest where bears face off in daily head-to-head votes until one champion is left — 16 bears are competing this year.
WHERE: Katmai National Park, 4.1 million acres of volcanoes, rivers, and forests in Alaska.
WHY: Bears need lots of fat to get through the long, cold winter, and the contest gets people excited about the park's bears.

perspectives.description: Fans love voting each day and cheering for their favourite bear, like Chunk, Bucky, or the mum with three cubs.
Rangers and scientists say the contest is a fun way to teach people about bears and about protecting the park.
Some people think it is just a silly internet game, and joke that the bears do not even know they are in a contest.
